chapter: Back to the horn: house sessions
title: Playing with Raymond Burke
summary: He likes the drive of Raymond's clarinet and the old tunes at the sessions.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Churchy used to play a lot of unusual numbers at those sessions. Yeah. What's it? Brown eyes?

Where are you- why are you blue? Raymond alone, man, he'll go back further than that. Memories and tunes like that, man. Weird. Old times. I used to like those sessions, though. Bring you back to old times, man. I like to play with Raymond. Me too. Don't you? Yeah. He's got a drive, man. I tell you, clarinet players will come and go, but Raymond, when he's feeling good, man, he can really kick a tempo. Make you feel it. Yeah. That's what it takes, Paul. A trombone and a clarinet, man, you're sitting in between two men like that. You've got to play. You've got to go, man. You can't drag. But when you get one weak man, you know, you just don't feel it. When you make something, you get a bone man who pulls that in at you. You've got to go. Or a clarinet man will make a lick like Raymond will make at you. He was making some nice licks the other night over there. Sure was. He's feeling good. Yeah. Y'all played a few old tunes there the other night. Yeah. We're going to get some more, too. Yeah. Yeah. Some of them old ones are good tunes.
